credentials.description: service ID — the user part of HTTP Basic auth, base64(SERVICE_ID:SECRET_TOKEN)
secret token — the password part of HTTP Basic auth

example_prompt: Add phone number verification via SMS to my signup flow.

sender_name.description: Sender name (case-sensitive, required). Must be a sender name with status 'accepted'. For WhatsApp, the Nimba SMS sender name can be used by default.

message.description: Message template. Must contain the <1234> placeholder, which will be replaced by the code. Default: 'Code de confirmation Nimba SMS <1234>'. For WhatsApp, the content is replaced according to the template.

expiry_time.description: Code validity period in minutes. Between 5 and 30 (inclusive). null by default.

attempts.description: Maximum number of attempts before expiry. Between 3 and 10 (inclusive). null by default.

code_length.description: Length of the generated code. Between 4 and 8 (inclusive). Default: 4.

verificationid.description: Unique verification identifier. Keep it to call verify_code.

code.description: Generated confirmation code (returned in the response to make testing easier).

message_cost.description: Number of SMS consumed. Always 1 for verifications.

expiry_time.description: Validation errors on the 'expiry_time' field (value outside the 5-30 range).

attempts.description: Validation errors on the 'attempts' field (value outside the 3-10 range).

code_length.description: Validation errors on the 'code_length' field (value outside the 4-8 range).

gotchas: sender_name is REQUIRED (not optional) and case-sensitive. Use list_sendernames to retrieve the names with status 'accepted'.
The <1234> placeholder in 'message' is required — without it, the code will not be included in the SMS. The text around the placeholder is free-form.
The identifier field in the response is 'verificationid' (not 'id'). Store this field server-side to call verify_code.
expiry_time and attempts are sent as null when not provided — the API applies its own internal defaults.
The generated code is returned in the API response ('code' field) — never expose it client-side; use it only for testing.
For WhatsApp (channel: 'whatsapp'), the message content is replaced according to a NimbaSMS template — the 'message' field is ignored.
open_questions: Sandbox: provider.json declares none and no gotcha documents a test environment — every call reaches production.
